es: Expresar una molestia con un mensaje en primera persona, pedir un cambio con Would you mind + -ing y disculparte sin retirar tu necesidad.

teaching.es: Me siento cansada cuando la música suena alta después de medianoche, porque empiezo a trabajar temprano y necesito dormir.

origin.text: Sara's flatmate keeps taking her charger without a word. She writes: I feel upset when my charger is not in my room. Would you mind ___ me before you borrow it?

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué cambió la conversación con su compañero.

choices.text: She said that she would move out unless he stopped playing the piano.
She asked him to practise the piano in a different flat.
She apologised for shouting, then described her feeling and made a polite request.

feedback.es: Lo que cambió fue pasar del grito a un mensaje con emoción, hecho y una petición cortés.

origin.audio: Last month I had a problem with my flatmate. He practised the piano every night until midnight, and I was exhausted. At first I shouted, which only made things worse. Then I apologised for raising my voice and told him how I felt: I feel tired when the noise goes on after ten, because I start work early. Would you mind playing earlier in the day? He said he had not realised, and we agreed on quiet hours. Now we are friends again.

prompt.es: Escribe una queja sin culpar con una petición cortés.

answer.text: I feel frustrated when your bags are in the hallway, because I need to get my bike out. Would you mind moving them after dinner?
accepted: I feel frustrated when your bags are in the hallway, because I need to get my bike out. Would you mind moving them after dinner?
I feel annoyed when you leave your bags in the hallway, because I need space for my bike. Would you mind putting them in your room?

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje nombra la emoción, el hecho y la necesidad, y termina con una petición cortés con Would you mind + -ing.

origin.text: Tu vecino deja sus bolsas en el pasillo y no puedes sacar la bici. Escribe un mensaje: di cómo te sientes y cuándo, por qué lo necesitas y pide un cambio con Would you mind.

prompt.es: Completa: «Gracias por ser sincero conmigo; sé que no era fácil decirlo.»

feedback.es: Be honest with someone es la colocación para hablar con sinceridad, incluso cuando cuesta.

origin.text: Tom told Sara that he had taken her charger again. Sara was not angry. She said: Thank you for being ___ with me; I know that was not easy.

prompt.es: Escribe la conversación de ocho turnos entre compañeros de piso.

answer.text:
Sara: Tom, I feel tired when the music is loud after midnight, because I start work very early. Would you mind turning it down after ten?
Tom: I'm sorry, Sara. I didn't realise it was a problem. If only I had asked you earlier how you felt.
Sara: Thanks for being honest with me. I'm sorry I had to raise my voice last week, but I do need some quiet hours during the week.
Tom: I understand, and I appreciate that you told me. I also feel upset when my speaker is not in my room. Would you mind asking me before you borrow it?
Sara: Of course. Next time I'll ask first. I wish I had asked you before I took it.
Tom: Thank you. Let's agree on quiet hours after ten, and I promise to keep the music low.
Sara: Agreed. I promise to own up to it whenever I forget something.
Tom: Deal. Let's check in again on Sunday and see if the plan works.

Leo: Ana, I feel stressed when the kitchen is messy after dinner, because I need a clean space to cook. Would you mind washing the dishes before you go out?
Ana: I'm sorry, Leo. I wish I had done it earlier. If only I had more time in the evening!
Leo: I understand, and I'm sorry I had to raise my voice yesterday. I do appreciate your help at the weekend, but I need some quiet hours to study.
Ana: Thanks for being honest. I also feel tired when I come home late, so would you mind sharing the chores with me?
Leo: Not at all. Let's agree on a plan: I cook on Mondays and you wash up on Tuesdays.
Ana: I promise to tell you if I am going to be late. From now on, we will speak honestly.
Leo: Deal. I will ask before I borrow your things, and I will own up to it if I forget.
Ana: Great. Let's check in again next Sunday, and we can change the plan if it does not work.

feedback.es: Un buen diálogo combina queja en primera persona, petición cortés, disculpa equilibrada, wish o if only y un acuerdo final.

origin.text: Escribe una conversación de ocho turnos (unas 150–240 palabras) entre dos compañeros de piso. Uno se queja con un mensaje en primera persona y pide un cambio con Would you mind; el otro se disculpa; al menos uno usa wish o if only; y acuerdan una solución.

prompt.es: Escucha el final de la conversación y elige qué actitud muestran los dos.

choices.text: Both accept part of the responsibility and want to repair the relationship.
Only Tom accepts responsibility, while Sara keeps her demand and says nothing more.
Both decide to avoid the subject to keep the peace.

feedback.es: Tom se disculpa y cambia su conducta; Sara reconoce que gritar no estuvo bien: los dos asumen su parte.

origin.audio: Tom listened while Sara explained how she felt. He did not interrupt. When she finished, he said: I'm sorry, Sara. I can see why you are upset. I wish I had noticed earlier. I'll keep the volume low after ten. Sara smiled and answered: Thank you. I'm also sorry that I raised my voice last week. I was tired, but that was no reason to shout.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se puede poner un límite sin atacar: necesito algunas horas de silencio.»

feedback.es: Set a boundary significa poner un límite claro y respetuoso, sin culpar a la otra persona.

origin.text: It is possible to set a ___ without attacking anyone. I do need some quiet hours at night, and I am saying so calmly.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Ana y elige cuál es su postura.

choices.text: She drops her complaint to avoid another argument.
She apologises for her tone but keeps her request.
She blames Leo for the way the rota was designed.

feedback.es: Ana se disculpa por levantar la voz, pero mantiene su petición de cambiar los turnos: disculpa equilibrada.

origin.text: Ana's message to Leo: I know the rota was my idea, and I'm sorry I raised my voice yesterday. Still, I feel tired when I do the dishes three nights in a row. Would you mind swapping with me on Thursdays? I promise to cook on Sundays, because I want us to be fair.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consigue Mia con su respuesta a las bromas de su compañero.

choices.text: She proves that he has been taking her clothes for weeks.
She accepts his joke and drops the subject for now.
She makes him take the problem seriously without starting a fight.

feedback.es: Mia mantiene la calma, dice cómo se siente y pide algo concreto: él deja de reírse y promete preguntar.

origin.audio: When Mia asked her flatmate to stop borrowing her clothes, he laughed and said it was no big deal. Mia did not shout. She said she felt upset when things disappeared from her room, and she asked him to check first. He stopped laughing and promised to ask.

prompt.es: Lee la situación y elige la disculpa equilibrada que Leo debería decir.

choices.text: I'm sorry I raised my voice, but I still need quiet hours at night.
I'm sorry you feel that way, and I will never mention it again.
I apologise, but honestly it was your fault that I raised my voice at all.

feedback.es: La disculpa equilibrada pide perdón por la propia parte y mantiene la necesidad; las otras la retiran o culpan.

origin.text: Leo shouted at his flatmate about the noise last night. Today he wants to apologise without pretending that the problem does not exist. He thinks about what to say.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo siento, levanté la voz, pero sí necesito silencio por las noches.»

feedback.es: But une la disculpa con la necesidad que se mantiene: pides perdón sin retirar lo que necesitas.

origin.text: Sara apologises without dropping her need. She says: I'm sorry I raised my voice, ___ I do need some quiet at night.
